learning_objective: 🎯 Explore what binds people together as a nation, the powerful demand for self-determination, and the dangers of aggressive nationalism!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A nation is not just a territory. It is an 'imagined community' held together by shared beliefs, historical memories, common political identity, and sometimes shared culture or language.

The right of a nation to govern itself and determine its own political future. This principle led to the breaking of empires and the creation of independent nation-states (like India from British rule).
While nationalism can unite people to fight oppression, aggressive nationalism can lead to war, hatred of minorities, ethnic cleansing, and the forceful assimilation of different cultures.

Modern democracies recognize that a state can have multiple cultures. Instead of 'one culture, one state', they embrace pluralism—respecting minority rights while building a shared political identity.
Indian nationalism was built on anti-colonialism and inclusive civic identity (democracy and constitution), rather than a single religion or language.

fun_activity.title: 🗺️ Build a Nation
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are starting a brand new country on an island. You have people speaking 3 different languages. To create a strong sense of 'Nationalism' without being unfair, what shared symbols or values will you create to unite them?

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly define a 'nation' as an imagined political community, distinct from a state (which is a legal/political entity).
📌 Understand the principle of 'National Self-Determination' and why it cannot be granted to every single cultural group today (it would lead to endless fragmentation).
📌 Contrast exclusive nationalism (based on religion/race) with inclusive/civic nationalism (based on shared political values).
quick_recap: ⭐ The idea of the nation-state emerged in Europe in the 19th century.
⭐ Shared beliefs, a common history, and a shared territory are key elements that constitute a nation.
⭐ Accommodating diversity (pluralism) is essential to keep a modern nation united and prevent separatist movements.
